atomicity.reason: Two independently violable behaviours: classify a reading invalid (more than 250 mV from the module median) and never use an invalid reading to evaluate a limit; the architecture allocates them to different elements (acquisition marks, supervisor ignores) and only the acquisition element traces to this requirement.
atomicity.suggestion: Split into a classification requirement and an exclusion requirement (tracing the supervisor to the latter), or keep one and trace both elements.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: module, median, cell voltage and the 250 mV window are stated or ordinary vocabulary, and the purpose is given.

feasibility.reason: A median-deviation check is easy to implement, but it cannot tell a failed sensor from a genuine outlier: a real cell more than 250 mV from its module median (for example a weak cell pushed past the overvoltage limit at end of charge) is classed invalid and never evaluated, which conflicts with REQ_CELL_VOLTAGE_LIMITS ('a single cell outside the range is sufficient') and the story's 'any cell'.
feasibility.suggestion: Add a fail-safe path so plausibility can suppress sensor faults but not real excursions, e.g. an implausible reading beyond an absolute limit still raises a fault or opens the contactors after N cycles, and a persistently invalid cell is itself reported.

parent_fit.reason: It is an enabling data-quality rule rather than part of the disconnect behaviour US_CELL_PROTECTION asks for: the story never mentions sensor failure or nuisance-trip avoidance, and by excluding outlier cells from limit evaluation the rule narrows the story's 'any cell' guarantee.
parent_fit.suggestion: Trace it to a story or feature that states measurement integrity, or extend US_CELL_PROTECTION to say protection decisions rely on plausible measurements, and state how a persistently invalid cell is handled so a real outlier is not silently ignored.

unambiguity.reason: The closing clause 'so a single failed sensor cannot by itself command the contactors open' reads as a guarantee the rule cannot deliver (a stuck or drifting sensor within 250 mV of the median still trips a limit, since REQ_CELL_VOLTAGE_LIMITS says one cell is sufficient), and 'failed sensor' and 'a cell-protection limit' do not say that only cell-voltage readings and voltage-based limits are covered.
unambiguity.suggestion: Reword the clause as non-normative rationale (or drop it) and state that the exclusion applies to the voltage-based limits only.

verifiability.reason: The core rule is exact and bench-checkable: |V_cell - median of its module| > 250 mV marks the reading invalid, and an invalid out-of-limit reading must not command the contactors open; threshold, unit, strict comparison and reference value are all stated.

summary: Precise 250 mV module-median rule, but it is an enabling rule only loosely tied to the story, bundles classification with exclusion, and can mask a genuine single-cell excursion.
